Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting a large discrepancy in DA magnitude between NAc (~90-fold) and LH (~2-fold) that may confound kinetic interpretations, questioning whether this reflects fiber density or baseline differences.

Both address speculative/hypothetical claims (C99, C105-C106, C110-C111, C114-C115, C126, C128, C137-C138). OpenEval categorizes these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are explicitly presented as hypotheses requiring experimental testing. Peer reviewers similarly view these as UNCERTAIN, requesting causal experiments to validate mechanistic conclusions.

Both evaluate main conclusions (C9-C10, C120, C135, C139-C141). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by collective experimental findings, though noting some involve inference beyond direct observation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the data are 'largely correlative' and requesting causal manipulation experiments (e.g., blocking orexin recruitment, testing raclopride effects on learning) to strengthen mechanistic claims.

Both address pharmacological experiments (C42, C70-C74, C76, C96, C103-C104). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and statistical analysis, acknowledging partial D2R effects. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation, citing methodological concerns: 5-minute drug absorption time is too short (literature suggests 30 minutes), requesting dose-response data and noting premature conclusions about receptor involvement.

Both evaluate VTA-LH dopamine findings (C5, C38, C51-C54, C58, C86). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by anatomical and functional data in Figure 3, with justified RPE encoding conclusions. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming findings as 'valuable' with 'solid evidence' and 'technically sound' experiments, with no substantive critiques of these core dopamine release findings.

Both evaluate orexin activity findings (C64-C67). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting gradual increase paralleling dopamine dynamics with high specificity (>96%). Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting that 'orexin neurons in LH mirrors that of LH DA levels' without challenge to the technical approach or temporal correlation.

Both address behavioral paradigm validation (C37, C43-C45, C48-C49). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by Figures 1-2 with appropriate statistical analyses, replicating prior work and validating discrimination. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, describing experiments as 'technically sound' with 'conclusions mostly reasonable,' affirming the behavioral findings shed light on reward-related learning.

Partial overlap on orexin-dopamine correlation (C7-C8, C40-C41, C95). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by Figure 5 data showing parallel dynamics. Peer reviewers rate these claims UNCERTAIN within broader pharmacological concerns, emphasizing correlative nature and requesting causal experiments to test whether dopamine recruitment of orexin is necessary for learning.

Both address omission trial responses (C55-C57, C68, C127). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting reasonable inferences about tonic dopamine and negative RPEs, with plausible hypotheses about sensor kinetics explaining lack of orexin dip. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, explicitly noting 'orexin neurons do not exhibit a decrease in activity in omission trials' as an established finding.

Minimal overlap on cue discrimination claims (C46-C47). OpenEval finds behavioral data SUPPORTED as part of paradigm validation. Peer reviewers accept omission-related observations without challenge, treating these as established findings within their broader evaluation.

Both address persistence of calcium signals after raclopride (C103-C104). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by Figure 6E data, noting this reveals complexity requiring further investigation. Peer reviewers include these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of pharmacological experiments, citing methodological concerns about drug timing and dose-response.

Both address dopamine-orexin dissociation during omission (C127, C136). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by experimental data showing dopamine dips but no orexin dip, with justified RPE encoding conclusions. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, treating the absence of orexin decrease in omission trials as an accepted observation.
